shipped_promises_as_verified.new_device_history: NONE. A send fans out one Olm envelope per recipient device that exists AT SEND TIME; the list endpoint returns only envelopes addressed to the caller's devices. A device added later is addressed in nothing earlier, so it starts empty. No recovery key, no key backup, no device-to-device history share, no cross-signing exists in either repo.
shipped_promises_as_verified.key_persistence: The Olm account is pickled under a random 32-byte pickle key in IndexedDB database `vidra-e2ee`, store `device`, key `self`, alongside a decrypted-message cache and a sent-message outbox. It survives a hard reload, a full browser restart and a sign-out/sign-in on the same browser. Clearing the origin loses the device and every message it could read.
shipped_promises_as_verified.recovery: None ships. Losing a browser's storage is unrecoverable by design (device-bound; the setup copy says so).
shipped_promises_as_verified.device_visibility: GET /e2ee/devices returns the caller's own devices. GET /users/{id}/e2ee/devices returns another user's device ids, names, PUBLIC identity and signing keys and timestamps, and ONLY to a caller who shares a conversation with them — an outsider and even the instance admin get 404. The one-time-key COUNT endpoint is owner-only: a conversation peer gets 404. Claiming prekeys is conversation-gated the same way. No private key is ever exposed by any endpoint.
shipped_promises_as_verified.server_visible_metadata: sender and recipient account ids and usernames, the conversation id and its dm_key (which literally names both participants), per-envelope created_at, ciphertext length, Olm message_type, device ids, user-chosen device NAMES, device public keys, last_seen_at, conversation updated_at/last_message_at, unread counts, and the fan-out width — one envelope row per recipient device, which reveals how many devices each party has.
shipped_promises_as_verified.attachment_rejection: 422 in every shape. Uploading into an encrypted conversation is refused BEFORE the multipart body is read: 422 'attachments are not supported on encrypted conversations'. A send carrying attachment_ids with envelopes is 422 on field attachment_ids with the same message; a send carrying attachment_ids without envelopes is 422 on field envelopes ('this conversation is encrypted; send envelopes, not body'). No attachment row and no stored bytes result.
